transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Ollie Chen (Redwood Product), Sofia Ramos (Beacon - Head of Search), Ethan Park (Beacon - ML Eng), Lina Gomez (Beacon - Security), Tom Barker (Beacon - Product)

--- Summary (auto) ---
Redwood demo of hosted API and Console focusing on embeddings + reranking flow for product search. Customer currently uses Elastic with a small embedding rerank prototype; they want better relevance for long-tail queries and faster iteration. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated capacity, prefix/KV cache benefits, expected QPS and batch sizing, and compliance needs. Action items and POC plan agreed.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:05] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm Jordan at Redwood, ae for retail accounts, and i'll run the first part — maya will jump into a demo of the embeddings and rerank endpoints and then show the console optimize recommendations.
[00:00:18] Sofia Ramos: Great thanks Jordan, appreciated. Quick note we have Ethan and Lina on from eng/security — i'm Sofia, heads of search. we run Elastic Cloud right now and have a small emb rerank prototype using a third-party embedder.
[00:00:30] Jordan Lee: Perfect, can you share quickly your primary goals? Is it relevance for long-tail, speed, cost, or a combo?
[00:00:36] Sofia Ramos: Primarily better relevance on product facets and long tail — customers searching for niche SKUs. But we also care about 95th percentile latency — our goal is sub 200ms for user facing results. Cost is a factor but accuracy first for now.
[00:00:50] Ethan Park: And from infra perspective we need to know if we can keep data in eu-west and we have SSO + strict audit requirements.
[00:00:58] Jordan Lee: Yep, got it. Hosted can be region pinned (we have eu-west endpoints) or Dedicated/Private for stricter residency. Maya, take it away on the demo.
[00:01:07] Maya Patel: Cool — i'll share my screen. i'll start with the embeddings API. So here you call POST /v1/embeddings with your model and text payload, you get back a vector — typical JSON. then for rerank we have our rerank endpoint which accepts a query embedding and a list of candidate doc embeddings or doc ids and returns scores or a sorted list. i'll run a quick example against a small product snippet set.
[00:01:34] [screen share noises]
[00:01:36] Maya Patel: Example request — we use batching by default on hosted to improve throughput; you can set batch_hint and prefer_latency flags if you want lower latency. note: batching and kv cache interact, so if you're doing very short queries you can get good p95s.
[00:01:52] Ethan Park: sorry quick clarif, you said KV cache — is that the key value cache for autoreg logits or for embeddings?
[00:01:58] Maya Patel: good question — that's our prefix/KV cache for llm KV cache, more important for generation. for embeddings/rerank we have a separate candidate cache and result cache patterns. i sometimes say KV cash haha — speech to text artifacts.
[00:02:10] Sofia Ramos: Heh yeah i've seen that in transcripts. Back to rerank — do you do cross-encoder style scoring or is it dot-product re-ranking?
[00:02:18] Maya Patel: We support vector-based dense rerank (dot product) and also a lightweight cross-encoder option for more accuracy but higher latency and compute. For production we often do a two-stage approach: ANN retrieval (your Elastic) -> embedding dot-product re-rank -> optional cross-encoder re-score for top-k.
[00:02:34] Tom Barker: How intrusive is that into our stack? we want minimal changes ideally.
[00:02:38] Jordan Lee: Minimal — most customers keep Elastic for recall and call our embeddings + rerank in the application layer as a post-retrieval step. We provide SDKs and examples.
[00:02:46] Maya Patel: here's the console — quick tour. On the Console you can run evals with labeled queries, test rerank quality metrics like MRR/ndcg, and see Optimize suggestions — batching sizes, quantization recommendations, and model variant tradeoffs. you can also flag a rollout to a canary traffic percentage.
[00:03:05] [00:03:07] Lina Gomez: On security — we need SOC2 type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS-managed customer keys for embeddings at rest. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[00:03:18] Maya Patel: We do — for Private and Dedicated we support KMS/HSM integrations, for Hosted we offer envelope encryption + bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options, and full audit logs. SOC2 attestation available; i'll attach the compliance pack.
[00:03:31] Lina Gomez: Good. Also want to confirm we can restrict access to logs and have retention controls.
[00:03:35] Jordan Lee: Yes, retention controls and token-level audit logs are possible — we'll include the security docs in follow up.
[00:03:41] Ethan Park: For throughput, what QPS can host handle for embeddings? we expect peaks of 120 qps for searches and ~600 qps for background indexing (downsampled).
[00:03:52] Maya Patel: For embeddings on Hosted we autoscale; typical single-tenant pool numbers vary by model. For your numbers you'd be fine on Hosted with some burst capacity; if you need guaranteed throughput and reserved latency you may want Dedicated. We can size a Dedicated pool — rough estimate: for 120 qps interactive you'd likely need X GPUs depending on model and sequence length, i'll put concrete numbers in the TCO sheet.
[00:04:12] Sofia Ramos: what's the p95 for a dot-product rerank stage?
[00:04:16] Maya Patel: The dot-product rerank is lightweight — p95 can be single-digit ms when you're just scoring in-memory vectors. The cross-encoder is the heavy one — p95 can go to 200-400ms depending on model/quantization unless you use an optimized variant.
[00:04:29] Jordan Lee: Important callout: Optimize recommendations in Console will suggest quantized model variants for cross-encoder to keep p95 acceptable and cost lower.
[00:04:37] [00:04:39] Ethan Park: Any guidance on batch sizes? our current batch logic is naive and stalls latency occasionally.
[00:04:44] Maya Patel: We recommend small micro-batches for interactive (4-16) and larger batches for background indexing. Also leverage prefix caching for repeated queries or top results caching. We'll share sample batching heuristics in the benchmark guide.
[00:04:58] Tom Barker: Do you have customers in retail using this flow?
[00:05:02] Jordan Lee: Yes — a few references, happy to connect — we ran a case where embeddings + rerank cut the number of poor relevance results by 30% and improved conversions. I'll include anonymized benchmarks.
[00:05:15] [00:05:17] Sofia Ramos: On cost, is there a ballpark per-1M query cost for embeddings + rerank on Hosted?
[00:05:23] Jordan Lee: Ballpark depends on model size — with our mid-tier embedder and dot-product rerank, you might expect $X-$Y per 1M queries; i'll send a detailed hosted vs dedicated TCO. note that caching and batching reduce the effective unit cost a lot.
[00:05:36] Lina Gomez: Data residency again — can we ensure embeddings never leave eu-west?
[00:05:41] Maya Patel: Yes — we can set regionally scoped endpoints and for Dedicated/Private you can have full VPC and on-prem options. We'll note it in the next steps.
[00:05:50] [00:05:52] Ethan Park: For the POC we want to run our labeled eval set — about 10k queries. can we push that and run against your hosted endpoints?
[00:05:59] Maya Patel: Absolutely. For a POC we often do 1) baseline with your current pipeline, 2) hosted embeddings + rerank, 3) hosted + optional cross-encoder top-k re-rank. we'll provide the eval harness and sample scripts.
[00:06:12] Jordan Lee: On timing, customer said they'd like to start POC in 2 weeks. is that feasible?
[00:06:16] Maya Patel: Yes — if we get the eval set and a technical kickoff we'll spin up test capacity and run the scripts.
[00:06:22] [00:06:23] Conversation — quick demo run through of API request/response and Console metrics, minor transcription gaps
[00:13:40] Maya Patel: ... so here's an example of the rerank payload — you can provide doc ids and we'll fetch cached vectors if you've indexed them with our ingestion tool; or you can pass vectors inline. both paths supported.
[00:13:55] Ethan Park: If we pass vectors inline do you store them? concerns about PII and retention.
[00:13:59] Maya Patel: Not unless you opt-in to indexing. Inline vectors are transient; retention and storage policies are configurable. We'll add that to security doc.
[00:14:06] Sofia Ramos: Great. Any offline indexing support? our catalog is large and we'd like to precompute embeddings.
[00:14:11] Maya Patel: Yes — you can use the batch embeddings endpoint for background indexing and then upload to your ANN or use Redwood's managed index product for Dedicated customers.
[00:14:20] Jordan Lee: Quick note about fallback strategies — if a heavy cross-encoder is slow we can route low-priority requests to dot-product only and reserve cross-encoder for checkout flows or high-value queries.
[00:14:33] Tom Barker: Makes sense.
[00:14:36] [00:14:40] Sofia Ramos: any specific infra changes needed? we prefer using our existing Elastic cluster and call Redwood via internal service.
[00:14:46] Maya Patel: No major infra changes — you'll call our API from your app tier. We'll share SDK examples in Node/Python and a Postman collection for quick integration.
[00:14:55] Ethan Park: Will you share a sample Postman with auth headers?
[00:14:58] Maya Patel: Yes, that's part of the POC pack.
[00:15:02] [00:15:05] Discussion of edge-case queries and how to construct prompt templates for cross-encoder
[00:18:30] Maya Patel: And on the Console Optimize tab here, you can see model recommendations based on your eval set — it suggests a quantized cross-encoder for lower cost and near-similar quality, and suggests a batching policy that balances p95 and cost.
[00:18:46] Sofia Ramos: Are there built-in monitors for regression? we want alerts if relevance drops after a model change.
[00:18:52] Maya Patel: Yes — you can create monitors on MRR/ndcg and set thresholds and alert channels. We also have versioned rollouts and automatic rollback policies if metrics degrade.
[00:19:03] Lina Gomez: OK the compliance pack and KMS details are the most important for security sign-off.
[00:19:08] Jordan Lee: We'll attach SOC2 report, ISO summary, SAML setup guide, and KMS integration doc in the follow up email.
[00:19:15] [00:19:17] Maya Patel: Last demo piece — rerank latency profiling. here's a trace showing dot-product scoring sub 10ms and cross-encoder at ~250ms for that particular model. if you push a quantized variant you can reduce that to ~120ms.
[00:19:35] Ethan Park: Nice, that helps.
[00:19:38] Jordan Lee: Cool — sounds like we have alignment on approach. Sofia, are the success metrics still improved NDCG by 10-15% and p95 <200ms on user flows?
[00:19:48] Sofia Ramos: Yes that's the internal target. Also reduced manual tuning for synonyms would be a plus.
[00:19:54] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick recap and next steps: 1) Jordan sends pricing + TCO, 2) Maya shares benchmark guide + eval harness, 3) schedule POC kickoff with Ethan/lina/infra, 4) customer confirms compliance docs needed. Anything to add?
[00:20:08] Tom Barker: Could we get a rough timeline for the POC steps in the follow up?
[00:20:12] Jordan Lee: Absolutely we'll include a proposed timeline — typically 2-4 weeks for a basic POC depending on integration complexity.
[00:20:18] Sofia Ramos: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:20:21] [00:20:25] Meeting winds down, small talk; call ends ~16:42 UTC
